problemStatement.formal: ∀ m n a b : ℤ, (∃ x, x ≡ a [ZMOD m] ∧ x ≡ b [ZMOD n]) ↔ ↑(Int.gcd m n) ∣ (a - b)
problemStatement.plain: Characterize the image of the natural map ℤ/mnℤ → ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ when gcd(m,n) ≠ 1. The system x ≡ a (mod m), x ≡ b (mod n) is solvable iff gcd(m,n) divides (a - b), and solutions are unique modulo lcm(m,n).
whyMatters: Completes the CRT picture beyond the coprime case
Characterizes which pairs (a,b) are in the image of the diagonal map
Fundamental result in number theory with applications to modular arithmetic

proven: Solvability criterion: system solvable iff gcd(m,n) | (a-b)
Explicit solution formula via Bézout coefficients
Coprime case reduces to standard CRT
